$comment: Lip sync v2 rules for lib/lipsync-text.mjs (author's prompt #15; rules changed after seeing output in prompts #16 and #17, see changedAfterSeeing). FROZEN since prompt #17 (rig/frozen.json). Chosen values, labelled so. Input: the character alignment ElevenLabs returns with the audio, letters with start and end times, not phonemes.

closure.why: lips together (m, b, p) or upper teeth on the lip (f, v): on this face both read as the closed smile

gap.why: spaces, punctuation and time no letter covers: the mouth at rest

f.why: upper teeth on the lower lip; Ping has no teeth, so F and V map to rest (step 1 decision)

o.why: o is said with rounded lips

u.why: u is said with rounded lips

e.why: e is said with spread lips

i.why: i is said with spread lips

y.rule: consonant at the start of a word before a vowel (you, yes), vowel everywhere else (my, very)
y.why: y before a vowel at a word start is a glide; elsewhere it is said like i or ee

onlyVowel.rule: when y is the only vowel letter of a word (no a, e, i, o or u): my, by, why
onlyVowel.why: said like 'I', which opens the jaw
onlyVowel.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #16, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "My" came out wide; it sounds like "I".

otherLetters.why: other consonants: tongue and teeth, mouth a little open

pairs.why: tongue between the teeth: a little open, not wide
mouth, sound, loud, wow: the sound starts open and ends round, so the first letter is open and the second round
pairs.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #16, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "mouth", "sound", "loud", "wow" came out round only; the sound starts open.

pairs.why: mouth, sound, loud, wow: the sound starts open and ends round, so the first letter is open and the second round
pairs.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #16, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "mouth", "sound", "loud", "wow" came out round only; the sound starts open.

pairs.why: each, read: said as ee, not as a
back of the tongue, mouth a little open; not two shapes

silentFinalE.rule: a word that ends in a consonant followed by e and has three or more letters, other than words ending in ee and the exceptions
silentFinalE.exceptionsWhy: the final e is said in these short words; found by a unit test before anything was rendered
silentFinalE.why: move, live: the final e is not said, so it must not spread the lips

pronounI.why: said like 'eye', which opens the jaw before it spreads

priorityWhy: since prompt #17 only for exact ties: when letters of two classes fall in one frame, the higher one wins: closures and roundings are the shapes a viewer misses most when they are skipped, an open jaw next; small is the default; gaps lose to any letter
minFramesRule: a run shorter than minFrames takes frames from the run after it if it outranks that run and that run would keep at least minFrames; otherwise it takes the mouth of the run before it (or after it at the start). Repeated until no run is shorter.
minFramesWhy: a mouth held for one frame at 30 fps reads as flicker (v1 had 4 to 6 such runs per phrase)

changedAfterSeeing.what: "My" came out wide; it sounds like "I".
changedAfterSeeing.change: y.onlyVowel: when y is the only vowel of a word (my, by, why), it is open.

changedAfterSeeing.what: "mouth", "sound", "loud", "wow" came out round only; the sound starts open.
changedAfterSeeing.change: pairs ou and ow: first letter open, second round; "you" and "your" stay round.

changedAfterSeeing.what: "moves" and "move" are rest for the whole word; "mouth" loses its open "o" the same way.
changedAfterSeeing.change: frameRule: a frame takes the character that covers most of its time; class priority only breaks ties. The minimum-run rule is unchanged.

rulesBefore: commit e2a7f56 (prompt #16), unchanged until prompt #17; npm run lipsync:compare reads it from git to show v2 before and after on the same audio

frameRule.rule: a frame takes the character that covers most of its time window; class priority only breaks exact ties. Spaces and punctuation compete like letters (their class is gap), and so does time no character covers (gap).
frameRule.readAs: Decided by Claude: the author's rule says 'the letter'; spaces and punctuation are read as characters that compete too, so a frame that is mostly a pause stays at rest, as it did before.
frameRule.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #17, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "moves" and "move" are rest for the whole word: a frame shared by two letters takes the higher-priority class, so the "o" between m and v keeps one frame and the minimum-run rule removes it. "mouth" loses its open "o" the same way.
frameRule.before: the highest-priority class among the characters overlapping the frame (rules up to commit e2a7f56)
